resources.string: Airi works with the Linux terminal built into Android. Turn on Linux development environment in Developer options, open the Terminal app and let it finish setting up. Airi carries on by itself after that.
Airi needs a small helper in Linux. Android doesn\'t let apps run commands there, so this takes one paste.
Set up Airi in Linux again
The helper in Linux was set up by a different install of Airi, so it won\'t talk to this one. Running the command again fixes that.
Tap the button below. It copies a command and opens the Terminal app.
In the terminal, touch and hold, tap Paste, then press Enter.
When a notification asks about port 47821, tap Allow always. You can also turn it on in the Terminal app\'s settings, under Security.
Already set up? Linux probably isn\'t running. Start it and Airi will find it.
Install a graphical app in the terminal and it shows up here. For example: sudo apt install gnome-calculator
Allow Airi to install apps, so that it can add this one to your launcher.
Couldn\'t add this app to your launcher.
Couldn\'t reach Linux. Open Airi to check that it\'s set up.
The helper in Linux belongs to a different install of Airi. Open Airi to set it up again.
The helper in Linux is out of date. Open Airi to update it.
